source.title: Plasticity and language in the anaesthetized human hippocampus

findings.method: Neuropixels probes in human hippocampus under propofol anesthesia (n=7, 651 neurons)
key_results: Hippocampal neurons detect auditory oddballs with improving accuracy over time (plasticity under anesthesia)
Real-time semantic encoding: 85.6% of units selective for 12 semantic categories
Syntactic encoding: 80% of units distinguish nouns vs non-nouns; 69.1% encode full POS taxonomy
Predictive coding: future-word decoding strength comparable to past-word (τ_future=0.840 vs τ_past=0.868)
Surprisal modulation present (contextual word probability affects firing rates)
Performance comparable to or exceeding awake EMU recordings on microwire electrodes
findings.model: E-I recurrent neural network reproduces emergent oddball plasticity via local circuit dynamics

c9_integration.cluster_1_quantum_foundations: Local computation without global integration mirrors decoherence-free subspaces
c9_integration.cluster_3_quantum_info: Predictive coding as effective information transfer; surprisal as local entropy production
c9_integration.cluster_6_neuromorphic: E-I RNN validates SNN/reservoir approach; hippocampus as biological reservoir
c9_integration.cluster_8_consciousness: Empirical support for IIT (Φ requires integration) and Global Workspace (consciousness = broadcasting)

limitations: Single anesthetic (propofol) — may not generalize to sleep, coma, ketamine, dexmedetomidine
Single region (hippocampus only) — no PFC, thalamus, or brainstem recordings
Epilepsy cohort — drug-resistant TLE may alter baseline physiology
Prediction vs contextualization ambiguity — future-word decoding may reflect statistical co-occurrence rather than active generation
implications: Sophisticated cognition can proceed without consciousness
Consciousness arises from inter-regional communication, not local computation
Validates 'layered autonomy' model: subsystems maintain competence when integrating layer is disrupted
Speech prosthetic potential for stroke/damage patients using hippocampal signals
